teams.name: Core Exec Team
teams.description: Default leadership and engineering team for bootstrapping a Paperclip company with a CEO, CTO, QA Engineer, starter project, and a recurring CEO heartbeat review task.

teams.name: Product Design
teams.description: Bundled product design team with a Principal Product Designer who owns wireframes, design critiques, and UX quality reviews for a product company.

teams.name: Product Engineering
teams.description: Bundled engineering team that pairs a CTO with a senior coder and a QA engineer to deliver, review, and verify product changes.

teams.name: Content Machine
teams.description: Optional content operations team with a lead agent, a recurring review task, and a vendored local content planning skill.

teams.name: Bookkeeper
teams.description: Reads your Stripe payments (and optionally Xero) to send a plain weekly summary of revenue and spending, monthly close notes, and early warnings about anything unusual. Strictly read-only.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Read-only weekly summaries of your revenue and spending

requiredApps.why: Reads your payments, refunds and payouts to report revenue. The bookkeeper only reads; it never charges, refunds or moves money.
Reads your invoices, bills and bank transactions for a fuller picture of spending. The bookkeeper only reads.

setupQuestions.prompt: Which day should the weekly summary arrive?

options.label: Monday
options.description: Start the week knowing how the last one went.

options.label: Friday
options.description: Close the week with the numbers.

setupQuestions.prompt: Which currency should totals be reported in?
setupQuestions.helpText: Use a three-letter code such as USD, EUR or GBP. Amounts in other currencies are shown as they are, with a note.

teams.name: Coding agent
teams.description: Works on your GitHub repository — sorts new issues every weekday, fixes bugs, opens pull requests with tests for you to review, and checks dependencies and project health every week.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Triages GitHub issues, fixes bugs and opens pull requests for review

requiredApps.why: Reads your repository and issues, and opens pull requests. Merging, pushing to your main branch, deleting branches and closing issues wait for your approval.

setupQuestions.prompt: Which GitHub repository should the coding agent work on?
setupQuestions.helpText: Type it as owner/name, for example acme/website. If you leave the suggestion, the agent lists your repositories and asks you to pick one.
setupQuestions.initialText: Our main repository (ask me which one)

setupQuestions.prompt: How should changes reach your main branch?

options.label: Open pull requests, never push to main
options.description: Every change is a pull request you review and merge.

options.label: Push small fixes to main
options.description: Typos, comments and one-line fixes go to main once you say yes to each one. Everything else is a pull request.

setupQuestions.prompt: How are the tests run?
setupQuestions.helpText: For example: npm test, pnpm test, pytest, go test ./...

outwardActions.label: Merging and pushing to the default branch

teams.name: Content creator
teams.description: Plans and writes social posts and blog articles in your voice, on a steady schedule, and publishes them only after you approve.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Plans, writes and publishes your posts on a steady schedule

requiredApps.why: Publishes your social posts. Without it, posts are drafted for you to copy and post yourself.
Publishes blog articles to your website. Without it, articles are drafted for you to publish yourself.

setupQuestions.prompt: Who are your posts for?
setupQuestions.helpText: Describe the people you want to reach, in your own words.
setupQuestions.initialText: People who could become our customers, and the customers we already have

setupQuestions.prompt: How should your posts sound?

options.label: Friendly
options.description: Warm and approachable, like talking to a regular customer.

options.label: Professional
options.description: Clear and polished, like a trusted adviser.

options.label: Playful
options.description: Light and fun, with a bit of humour.

setupQuestions.prompt: How often should you post?

options.label: 2 posts a week
options.description: Steady and easy to keep up.

options.label: 1 post a week
options.description: A light, regular presence.

options.label: Every weekday
options.description: Five posts a week, for fast-moving audiences.

teams.name: Email secretary
teams.description: Sorts your inbox every morning, drafts replies in your voice, flags what is urgent, and sends you a short end-of-day digest.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Sorts your inbox, drafts replies and sends a daily digest

requiredApps.why: Reads your email and prepares replies. With Gmail, replies are saved as drafts for you to send; with AgentMail, they can be sent after you approve.
Checks when you are free if an email asks for a meeting.

setupQuestions.prompt: What should your secretary call you?
setupQuestions.helpText: Used in your digests and to sign drafted replies.

setupQuestions.prompt: When should the morning inbox sweep run?

options.label: 8am on weekdays
options.description: Ready when most working days start.

options.label: 7am on weekdays
options.description: For early starts.

options.label: 9am on weekdays
options.description: Catches the early-morning email too.

setupQuestions.prompt: What counts as urgent for you?
setupQuestions.helpText: Urgent email is flagged to you straight away instead of waiting for the digest.

outwardActions.label: Accepting meetings or changing your calendar

teams.name: Newsletter editor
teams.description: Researches, writes and schedules your email newsletter on a steady cadence, through Beehiiv, Resend or Klaviyo, after you approve each issue.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Researches, writes and schedules your newsletter on time

requiredApps.why: Holds your subscriber list and sends each issue.

setupQuestions.prompt: What is your newsletter about?
setupQuestions.helpText: Say what subscribers should get from each issue.
setupQuestions.initialText: News, tips and offers from our business for our customers

setupQuestions.prompt: How often should an issue go out?

options.label: Weekly
options.description: Keeps you top of mind.

options.label: Every two weeks
options.description: Less work, still regular.

options.label: Monthly
options.description: A fuller round-up once a month.

setupQuestions.prompt: Which day should issues go out?

options.label: Tuesday
options.description: A common day for good open rates.

options.label: Thursday
options.description: Lands before the weekend.

teams.name: Researcher
teams.description: Watches your market and sends a short weekly brief on competitors, customers and trends, with sources and what it means for you.

staplesTemplate.tagline: A weekly brief on your market, competitors and customers

setupQuestions.prompt: What should the researcher keep an eye on?
setupQuestions.helpText: Your Company Brief already describes the business. Name the topics, competitors or customer groups that matter most right now.
setupQuestions.initialText: Our market: competitors, what customers want, and trends that could affect our business

setupQuestions.prompt: Which day should the weekly brief arrive?

options.label: Monday
options.description: Start the week knowing what changed.

options.label: Friday
options.description: Look back on the week before the weekend.

setupQuestions.prompt: How detailed should each brief be?

options.label: Brief
options.description: A five-minute read: the top few items and what they mean.

options.label: Deep dive
options.description: A fuller analysis with more background and more sources.

teams.name: Social media manager
teams.description: Plans a week of social posts every Monday, publishes each one on its day after you approve it, and checks comments and mentions every afternoon.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Plans your social posts each week and keeps an eye on replies

requiredApps.why: Publishes your posts and reads comments and mentions. Every post waits for your approval unless you turn on autopilot for posting.

setupQuestions.prompt: Where should your social media manager post?
setupQuestions.helpText: You can add the other one later.

options.label: LinkedIn
options.description: Best for reaching other businesses and professionals.

options.label: X
options.description: Short, frequent posts and quick conversations.

setupQuestions.prompt: How should your posts sound?

options.label: Friendly
options.description: Warm and approachable, like talking to a regular customer.

options.label: Expert
options.description: Knowledgeable and useful, sharing what you know.

options.label: Bold
options.description: Confident and direct, with strong opinions.

setupQuestions.prompt: How many posts a week?

options.label: 3 posts a week
options.description: Steady and easy to keep up.

options.label: 5 posts a week
options.description: One every weekday.

options.label: 7 posts a week
options.description: One every day if your platform can schedule posts; otherwise some weekdays get two.

teams.name: Support triage
teams.description: Checks your support inbox every two hours on weekdays, sorts customer messages, drafts friendly answers, and passes anything tricky to the right person.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Sorts customer messages, drafts answers and escalates problems

requiredApps.why: Where customer messages arrive. With Gmail, replies are saved as drafts for you to send; with AgentMail or Slack, they can be sent after you approve.

setupQuestions.prompt: In a few sentences, what do customers buy from you and what do they usually ask about?
setupQuestions.helpText: Your Company Brief covers the basics. Add the things customers ask about most: delivery, returns, opening hours, how to use the product.
setupQuestions.initialText: Our products and services as described in our Company Brief. Customers mostly ask about orders, delivery, returns and how things work.

setupQuestions.prompt: Who should handle refunds, complaints and questions the assistant cannot answer?
setupQuestions.helpText: Name the person. They get a task with a summary and a suggested reply.

setupQuestions.prompt: How should replies to customers sound?

options.label: Warm
options.description: Friendly and reassuring, like a helpful shop assistant.

options.label: Concise
options.description: Polite, short and straight to the answer.

teams.name: Website builder
teams.description: Builds a simple, good-looking website for your business, shares a preview link for you to review, and checks the live site every week.

staplesTemplate.tagline: Builds a simple website, shares previews and checks it every week

requiredApps.why: Hosts your site. Previews are shared with you first; publishing to your live site waits for your approval.

setupQuestions.prompt: What should your website do for your business?
setupQuestions.helpText: For example: get people to book a call, show your menu and opening hours, or collect sign-ups for a launch.
setupQuestions.initialText: Explain what we do and help visitors get in touch with us

setupQuestions.prompt: What style should the site have?

options.label: Clean
options.description: Simple, calm and easy to read. Lots of white space.

options.label: Bold
options.description: Big headlines, strong colours and confident wording.

options.label: Playful
options.description: Friendly colours, rounded shapes and a light touch.

setupQuestions.prompt: Which web address should the site use?
setupQuestions.helpText: If you already own a domain, type it here. Connecting it is a step you do at your domain provider; the builder writes the steps for you.
setupQuestions.initialText: use the free host address for now

outwardActions.label: Publishing to your live site
outwardActions.destructiveLabel: Deleting a site or deployment, or buying or moving a domain
